added: The runner cost draws from your account or organization's included compute usage. Additional usage is billed at standard GitHub Actions rates.

If you run a workflow on a standard Linux runner and it takes 10 minutes to complete, $0.06 USD is deducted from the repository owner's included compute usage (10 × $0.006 USD). If the workflow generates a 10 MB artifact, then you'll also use 10 MB of the repository owner's artifact storage allowance.

If you run a workflow that normally takes 10 minutes and it fails after 5 minutes because a dependency isn't available, the cost of 5 minutes is deducted from the included compute usage. If you fix the problem and re-run the workflow successfully, the total cost is based on 15 minutes.

The included compute usage is expressed as a monetary amount, not a fixed number of minutes or other usage units. Products measure usage in different units, such as minutes, seconds, or GiB-seconds, and apply the corresponding rate. GitHub deducts the calculated cost from the same included compute usage. As a guide, $300 USD covers 50,000 minutes on a standard Linux runner at $0.006 USD per minute.
For example, if your organization uses GitHub Team, 5,000 minutes after the included compute usage is consumed would cost $38 USD if you used baseline Linux and Windows runners.
